correctness.rationale: Every fixed excitation shell has a known flat rank-a input spectrum and target-excited dimension b. Ky Fan projector optimization gives min(a,b)q^k/(1+q)^n, and explicit sector permutations attain all bounds concurrently. The even/odd Pascal identities were proved including central coefficients; the Catalan generating function proves the sharp q=1/2 transition, and uniform Stirling-tail estimates prove the log-minus-3/2-loglog bath-size expansion with O(1) error. 509 exact-rational tests independently check finite sector ranks, recurrences, boundary q values and a physical example. Finite tests are not infinite proofs.

originality.rationale: Closest accessible published literature establishes the one-thermal-qubit obstruction, general finite-bath resource constraints, and distinct coherence/cooling protocols. It does not establish an identified implication-equivalent all-size parity/Catalan optimum or sharp critical-size divergence for a product of identical thermal qubits. The well-known sector majorization method itself and the n=1 obstruction are explicitly prior. Complete access limitations and an unindexed-specialization risk are material and recorded.

An unindexed prior identity for thermal qubit bath Catalan coefficients or an equivalent fixed-spectrum thermo-majorization optimization might cover the closed formula even without matching titles.

value.rationale: The natural thermal-bath resource question raised by single-qubit no-go and qutrit activation has a sharp answer for another elementary reservoir architecture: arbitrarily many identical thermal qubits. The result determines exactly which bath sizes can create nonpassive work, proves complete even-size resource redundancy, and quantifies minimal resource growth with a nontrivial logarithmic correction near the universal Boltzmann-factor boundary. These are operationally interpretable finite-reservoir cutoffs not obtained from correctness or computation alone.
